questions.stem: Which Indus Valley site, located on the Ravi river, was the FIRST to be discovered (1921)?
questions.explanation: Harappa (modern Sahiwal district, Punjab, Pakistan) — discovered by Daya Ram Sahni in 1921 under leadership of John Marshall (then ASI Director-General). Lent name to the entire 'Harappan Civilization' (preferred over IVC since sites span beyond Indus river). Located on the bank of the Ravi. Mohenjodaro (Larkana district, Sindh, Pakistan) — discovered next year, 1922, by R.D. Banerji. Carbon-dated mature phase: ~2600-1900 BCE.

questions.stem: The 'Great Bath' — most famous structure of the Indus Valley — is at:
questions.explanation: Great Bath at Mohenjodaro — 11.88 m × 7.01 m × 2.43 m deep. Probably used for ritual bathing. Made watertight using gypsum mortar, lime plaster, and bitumen layers. Located in the citadel area. Also at Mohenjodaro: 'Granary' (largest building), 'College of Priests', 'Assembly Hall', dancing-girl bronze statuette, priest-king bust. Layout follows the grid (chess-board) plan with Citadel + Lower Town. UNESCO WHS since 1980.

questions.stem: Lothal — famous for its dockyard (suggesting maritime trade) — is in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Lothal — Saragwala village, Gujarat. Excavated 1955-62 by S.R. Rao (ASI). World's earliest known TIDAL DOCK (~37 × 22 m, 4.5 m deep). Trade with Mesopotamia, Bahrain, Persian Gulf. Other Gujarat IVC sites: Dholavira (Kutch — UNESCO WHS 2021), Surkotada (with horse remains), Kuntasi, Rojdi. Indus's reach far beyond the Indus — modern India: 1,500+ sites identified; 6 are major (Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Dholavira, Rakhigarhi, Ganweriwal, Mehrgarh).

questions.stem: Rakhigarhi — currently being claimed as the LARGEST Harappan site by some excavators — is in which state?
questions.explanation: Rakhigarhi — Haryana, Hisar district. Estimated extent ~350 ha (older estimates put Mohenjodaro at ~250 ha). Excavations led by Vasant Shinde (Deccan College, Pune); ancient DNA from Rakhigarhi skeleton (paper 2019) showed strong Iranian-related component but NOT Steppe — important for the Aryan-migration debate. Government of India announced major site museum (under construction). 5 mounds identified (RGR-1 to RGR-5). Other major Haryana IVC sites: Banawali, Bhirrana (oldest?), Mitathal, Farmana.

questions.stem: Dholavira — the 4th Indian site to win UNESCO World Heritage status (2021) for IVC — is famous for:

options.option_text: Sophisticated water-management system + a 10-letter signboard inscription

questions.explanation: Dholavira — Kutch, Gujarat. Three-fold city plan (Citadel, Middle Town, Lower Town) — unusual. Sophisticated water-conservation: 16 reservoirs (rock-cut), check dams, channels. The 'Signboard' — 10 large symbols carved on wood, found near the gateway, possibly the world's earliest 'town signboard'. Indus script remains UNDECIPHERED. UNESCO WHS 2021. Lothal had the dockyard. Bronze 'Dancing Girl' is from Mohenjodaro.

questions.stem: Match Indus Valley site with its river — which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Kalibangan (Rajasthan, Hanumangarh district) is on the GHAGGAR (a dried-up river, identified with the mythical Saraswati) — NOT the Beas. Famous for: pre-Harappan + Mature-Harappan layers, ploughed field (oldest known), fire altars (suggesting ritual). Mohenjodaro on Indus, Harappa on Ravi, Lothal on Bhogavo. Banawali (Haryana) — also on Ghaggar. Manda (J&K) — northernmost site, on Chenab.

questions.stem: The famous 'Pashupati Seal' — depicting a horned figure surrounded by animals (often interpreted as proto-Shiva) — was found at:
questions.explanation: Pashupati Seal — found at Mohenjodaro by John Marshall in 1928-29. Steatite (soapstone) seal, cross-legged horned deity, surrounded by elephant, tiger, rhino, water buffalo. Marshall interpreted it as proto-Shiva 'Pashupati' (Lord of Beasts). Other interpretations: Asko Parpola sees a Vedic deity. Most IVC seals carry inscriptions in undeciphered Indus script + animal figures. Total Indus script signs: ~400-450 distinct characters.
